lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is a public board meeting where Telluride Regional Medical Center's board will take action — in public, after executive session — on who leads the hospital in the near term; if you care about local healthcare, that's the meeting to watch. Mountain Village is also moving an ordinance that would shift affordable housing fee-setting authority out of the municipal code, a structural change worth understanding. On top of that, HARC takes up a work session on potentially demolishing and replacing Rebekah Hall, the Town-owned building where it actually meets, and the BOCC continues discussions on constitutional amendments and a long-standing view-plain MOU involving Mountain Village.

notable.stake: Board votes publicly on interim hospital leadership after executive session.
Ordinance would move affordable housing fee-setting out of municipal code permanently.
Work session on demolishing and rebuilding Town-owned Rebekah Hall; public should track.
BOCC weighs constitutional amendments and a view-plain MOU with Mountain Village.
Two public hearings: a PUD application and a parcel subdivision in Ouray County.
